key_insight: DPA4C-LR combines long-range electrostatics and electrical-response prediction with spatially decomposable machine-learning interatomic potentials.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables large-scale atomistic modeling of field-dependent material behavior and interfacial thermal transport toward device-relevant length scales.
method: Separate electrostatic forces and Born effective charges into global electrostatics and strictly local derivatives of learned latent charges.
Preserve spatial decomposition for distributed evaluation of energies, forces, stresses, and electrical response.
Implement DPA4C-LR on nvalchemi with support for different electrostatic boundary conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports scaling to 5.2 million atoms on four GPUs at approximately twice the short-range backbone cost, plus demonstrations spanning water infrared spectra, relaxor hysteresis, ionic conductivity, and Si/diamond thermal transport.
watch_item: Global electrostatics and boundary-condition handling remain implementation concerns; the abstract does not establish scaling efficiency beyond four GPUs.
paper_title: Scalable long-range machine learning interatomic potentials with electrical response for atomistic material modeling
